headline: California's governor has signed a law barring hospitals and clinics from letting AI independently do medical work that needs a professional licence.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 4: the law was signed around 30 Sep 2026, before the window, and this is a later explainer with some new reaction.
importance_line: Patients in California and the nurses and doctors who treat them are affected from 1 Jan 2027, but it is unclear which current uses of AI the law would actually stop.
summary: The Press Democrat reports that California's AB 1979, signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom in late September and taking effect on 1 Jan 2027, bars hospitals and doctors' offices from using AI to carry out tasks that need a professional licence, such as prescribing medicines or ordering tests, and requires them to take reasonable steps so licensed staff can use their own judgment when AI tools guide care. The paper adds that it is unclear whether the law stops any AI use now in place, that the nurses' union that sponsored it says employers are already putting AI into nurses' work, and that Kaiser Permanente says its AI tools support clinicians rather than make care decisions.
notes: Read the Press Democrat in full. Older news re-dated: the signing was around 30 Sep 2026 (date taken from other outlets' listings, not opened); the Press Democrat piece adds reaction and the point that the law's reach is unclear. First time our edition carries AB 1979 itself.
